Glass was a joke.

I worked with a guy who had a set--must have been pre-beta or the "early adopter" release--and he just looked like an utter dork. I have never tried them though, so I can't comment on their effectiveness.

When Glass was pitched, wearables (I'm talking watches and such) were just a manufacturer's promise.

Now that they're here, and great (I have a Gear 2 and I LOVE it), Glass is simply irrelevant. What Google didn't figure is that somebody wouldn't want to wear something as cumbersome as Glass to have the same functionality (albeit, without augmented reality--which never really caught on) as a $200 wristwatch.

Technology, especially in this area, is moving at a frightening pace. It's OK though...we, the consumer, are the ultimate winners!

Glass fits in with the "Modren Man" concept, though.

Sure it's irrelevant now, but in fifty years when we have CPUs implanted into our wrists, touch-based keyboards embedded in our arms, etc. Glass-style systems will provide the visuals we'd need to be walking computers.

I just want a tactical network and a HUD. They could have taken what they used for their marketing disaster and refined it, in private.

Instead, we got another Sergey Brin overpromise and failure to understand product design.

I was looking forward to getting a live feed from an end user's glass and walking them through checking network cables or whatever.

Shame. Guess I'll have to file Glass with the flying cars and jetpacks.

Smaller communities are almost always better. This has a similar feel to how a lot of reddit was 7 or 8 years ago.

Some comedian (I think) put it best. It's far more difficult to be an asshole when you're living on an island with only a handful of people, because everyone is quickly able to spot the asshole and boot them out. The larger the community of the island gets though the more difficult it becomes to spot the assholes, because you don't know the other people in the community as well, and there are a lot more assholes. So the assholes are able to blend into the background more easily and cause more problems. When you have a community as large as reddit, it becomes almost impossible to spot the assholes, so people begin to segment themselves off into echo chambers filled with other people who are exactly like them, because if you can't always spot the assholes, at least you can be around people who think like you do a majority of the time.
